verdict.rationale: Svelte's official MCP server includes a svelte-autofixer tool that statically analyzes Svelte code and returns issues and suggestions to an AI agent. That is first-party AI-assisted code analysis, but nothing shows it inspects the component tree or targets rendering or reactivity performance. missing for 10: evidence of component-tree analysis, rendering/reactivity optimization suggestions, devtools-style runtime profiling integration, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native developer, I can use AI-powered devtools that analyze my component tree and suggest specific rendering or reactivity optimizations

citations.quote: svelte-autofixer: Analyzes Svelte code and returns issues and suggestions.
The Svelte MCP (Model Context Protocol) server can help your agent write better Svelte code. It works by providing relevant documentation, and statically analysing generated code
